body_long:
Four Seasons Resort Megève reopens on 16 December 2026 for the winter season, its first since receiving the Palace distinction. It is the first hotel in Megève to hold the title.

## A Palace in a ski village

Atout France granted the distinction in June 2026, for three years. The resort joins Four Seasons Hotel George V in Paris and Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat among the brand's Palaces in France. It is one of 33 Palaces in the country this year, six of them new.

Opened in 2017 on the Mont d'Arbois estate, the resort has 55 rooms and suites, including 14 suites, with direct access to the slopes. It counts three restaurants: La Brasserie Benjamin, Kaito and Idéal 1850, on the mountaintop. The hotel holds three Michelin Keys.

The estate was created under Ariane de Rothschild, on land that Noémie de Rothschild first imagined as a resort in 1920. General Manager Joachim Jacob, who joined the resort in 2019, leads the team. On the distinction, he said Four Seasons can "transform a stay into an experience shaped around each guest".

## What is new this winter

The novelty is in the 900-square-metre spa, one of the largest in the region. It now offers treatments by myBlend, the skincare brand created by Olivier Courtin-Clarins, Managing Director of the Clarins group. The resort also says it is the first in France to offer the CellSynergy2 device, which combines radiofrequency, ultrasound, electrostimulation and cryotherapy.

## The signal

The Palace label is no longer only a Paris or Riviera story. In a ski village, Four Seasons now uses its spa and its restaurants to give returning guests a reason to book again. Congratulations to the Megève team on its first winter as a Palace.
